title: A shared bath referent makes bodily entry a partial operation in complete GDT599 statements
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_WITH_KNOWN_COUNTERCASE. In the existing complete hypothetical GDT599 reader, S402 has HOLD(body in bath), REMOVE(same body), PUT_IN(same body), whereas S441 has HOLD(body in bath), PUT_IN(same body) without an intervening removal or explicit destination change. A shared physical bath plus strict state-changing entry licenses the first sequence and contradicts the second. This is a finite content commitment over existing complete statements, not a new word glossary or an independently established manuscript meaning. The known countercase should stop this strict conjunction without a large experiment if its bindings are verified.

new_content_contract.identity: Follow the existing explicit ANAPHORIC/source_pointer chain to the same physical body within each statement. Do not identify bodies across statements. Own/default definite participants are not globally unified merely by the same BODY class.
new_content_contract.container_binding: In a maximal local chain without an explicit directional destination change, bath in SH and omitted destination in K denote the same bath B. This is a NEW reference assumption. A changed grade alone does not introduce a new bath. An explicit source/target packet such as S442 must be retained; it cannot be flattened into the same-bath example.
new_content_contract.chronology: The existing ordered actual-action reading is strengthened to consecutive physical state constraints. No invisible withdrawal, fresh body, container replacement or event is inserted between consecutive BODY hosts. A habitual, normative or nonchronological interpretation is a serious rival, not silently included in this conjunction.
new_content_contract.shared_partial_operation: For one tracked body x and bound bath B, use occupancy i(x,B) in {OUT,IN}. HOLD_IN(x,B) requires IN and preserves IN. REMOVE(x,B) requires IN and yields OUT. Strict PUT_IN(x,B) requires OUT and yields IN. These are uniform functions/preconditions, not separate rules for each statement.
new_content_contract.directional_boundary: More generally strict placement at written destination B requires loc(x)!=B. An explicitly written FROM=A,TO=B additionally requires loc(x)=A; it need not pass through an unrepresented OUT event. S442 therefore cannot be rejected merely because its body was already in some bath. Distinctness or identity of A and B must be an explicit further binding; no outcome is claimed for the full S442 under the simple Boolean same-bath fragment.
new_content_contract.rest_of_statement: Non-body clauses and all controls retain their old content. The new occupancy fragment makes no fresh physical claim about their unspecified effects. The contradiction at S441 is between adjacent SH/BODY and K/BODY hosts, so it does not depend on assigning any earlier PORTION action a no-op effect. Later closure cannot undo a precondition violation. S442 P/BODY and CHD/BODY remain visible rather than being silently converted into no-ops or a validating endpoint.
new_content_contract.capacity: Zero new whole-word values, no new production, no fitted quantity, no per-occurrence exceptions. One Boolean occupancy state per bound body/bath chain suffices for the two decisive cells; HOLD fixes its input, so neither cell has a free initial-state bit. The global alternatives are strict placement versus idempotent destination assignment and same versus different implicit bath. Their choice is a semantic assumption, not a recovered manuscript value.

strongest_countercase_and_rival.known_countercase: S441 is already a direct countercase to strict physical entry PLUS shared implicit bath PLUS actual chronological action, if the frozen old BODY/reference assignments are retained. Do not run a large census as though this conjunction had no known counterexample. No part of GDT599 itself claimed this stronger occupancy law.
strongest_countercase_and_rival.strongest_scope_counterexample: S442 has a same-body SH-to-K chain WITH explicit source and target. An IN/OUT-only detector ignoring those arguments would produce a false conflict. The proposal must preserve the target/source distinction and refrain from a complete execution verdict where their identities or later P effects remain unbound.
strongest_countercase_and_rival.credible_rival: K can assign a desired placement or treatment state idempotently, or its omitted destination can differ from the previous bath. These are ordinary substantive alternatives to strict entry; a new container is not impossible merely because it is unexpressed. This proposal specifically tests the stronger shared-container/strict-entry conjunction.
strongest_countercase_and_rival.old_reader_limit: GDT590/591 body-first and episode-continuity observations selected role assignments under a guessed governor/blocker model; they were not independent body, bath, occupancy or chronology observations. GDT599 completes source/reference slots but its participant history is not an inside/outside state machine.
strongest_countercase_and_rival.relation_to_old_cards: IDEA000079 asks about serial idempotence versus additive output response and lacks measured before/after outcomes. This is not a successful execution of that original contract: it tests a NEW conditional partial-operation law using hypothesized occupancy predicates. IDEA000052 supplies broad identity/state distinctions but had no such concrete two-statement precondition contrast. W43's free stocks and times do not supply these occupancy facts and are not rerun.
strongest_countercase_and_rival.no_semantic_promotion: These deductions constrain a deliberately strengthened old hypothetical reading. They cannot confirm body, bath, temperature grades, treatment, K, CH, SH or any manuscript word. Confirmed words remain0.

smallest_decision_changing_review.first: Verify only the stored whole statements and exact host/reference chains at S402 and S441, preserving all modifiers; inspect S442 to ensure explicit destination changes are not erased. This proposal already carries their records and source hashes. A manual composition of three small partial-operation rules is enough; no decoder, new source or full313statement scan is warranted.
smallest_decision_changing_review.outcomes: If the reported immediate same-body/no-destination bindings are correct, close the strict common-bath conjunction with S441 as a conditional counterexample. If a written intervening removal or destination argument was omitted, correct the proposal's source claim rather than change the old reader. If the bath coreference cannot be defended, retain the explicit alternative and make no manuscript exclusion. A positive S402 alone never selects strict entry.
smallest_decision_changing_review.budget_includes: Primary verification, compact decision and publication if root selects; no software implementation is necessary.
smallest_decision_changing_review.no_automatic_repair: Do not respond to S441 by changing BODY to STATION, introducing another bath because of grade II, treating K as an exceptional no-op, or searching another paragraph. Any such alternative would be a different declared semantic candidate.
